args.summary: The latest deploy, v2.3.1, began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Rolled back all regions to the most recent release that was healthy in production, v2.3.0. Post-rollback status confirms all regions healthy on v2.3.0 with error rate ~0.2%. args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions

trace.final:
**Summary of what I did:**

1. **Diagnosed:** checkout-api was unhealthy in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) running v2.3.1 with an 18% error rate. Deployment history confirmed v2.3.1 was the failing deploy, and the most recent version that had ever been healthy in production was **v2.3.0** (v2.3.0 and v2.2.9 both healthy; the only other release, v2.3.1-rc, was staging-only and unhealthy).

2. **Rolled back:** Deployed v2.3.0 to all production regions. Post-rollback status check confirms all regions are now healthy on v2.3.0 with the error rate back down to ~0.2%. No change-manager approval was required since v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production.

3. **Opened incident:** Created **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer, documenting the v2.3.1 regression, the rollback to v2.3.0 across all regions, and the confirmed healthy post-rollback state. Follow-up noted: root-cause the v2.3.1 failure before re-deploying it.
